checks: The first-coordinate rank in the predecessor's triangular transport is common to the normalized endpoint laws. In upper rank the midpoint projection is the arithmetic average of their upper quantiles, and both marginal projections are nonatomic.

The midpoint event contains the intersection of the two endpoint events and lies in their union for every pair, since the midpoint margin is their average at the same tilt. Hence the integrand I_A+I_B−I_M has only values 0 and 1, including equality in the closed halfspaces.

The scaled B marginal contributes (a/b)U_B inside the coupling. Adding the unspent (1−a/b)U_B restores the actual endpoint mass. The events are nested initial rank intervals, so the midpoint probability is between min(p,q) and max(p,q). Proper thresholds are the exact inverses at their tail ranks.
Source §2 equations (5)–(6) give the exact same marginal normalization and limit the quantile equality to proper cuts.

dependencies.hypotheses: Apply with the first axis u/||u||, interpolation weight 1/2, and containing body (A+B)/2. Its conditional-quantile proof constructs a probability coupling with uniform marginals, monotone first-coordinate rank and absolutely continuous midpoint law. Multiply that probability law by a for the exact marginals.

overlap.comparison: The accepted width-based endpoint bound is for arbitrary actual cap volumes at one tilt. It does not decompose those volumes into common-rank midpoint contribution, unused B mass and the nonnegative exact indicator remainder.

The accepted proof constructs the directional coupling after a coordinate choice and gives its density and centroid. The stated endpoint accounting and rank-event identities are additional uses of that construction.
